item.title: Incarico post-doc: Regularity for solutions of partial differential equations with irregular coefficients (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-03 Analisi matematica, probabilità e statistica matematica

The research program analyzes how the regularity of coefficients affects the integrability and higher differentiability of solutions to nonlinear elliptic equations in divergence form, identifying quantitative estimates for higher-order gradient regularity even with discontinuous spatial dependence (Sobolev or Besov spaces). Starting from standard growth equations and local gradient estimates, the study will address non-standard growth problems and parabolic equations, identifying minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients and providing examples and counterexamples. Scientific supervisor: Prof. Antonia Passarelli di Napoli (Project "000022_BUDGET_ECONOMICO_RICERCA_2026").

item.title: Contratto di ricerca: The ubiquity of logarithmically correlated fields (ROMA "Tor Vergata")
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-15 23:59
Institution: ROMA "Tor Vergata", Roma, Rm
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-04 Fisica matematica

In 2012 Fyodorov, Hiary, and Keating formulated a striking conjecture: the maxima of log-determinants of large random matrices behave like those of logarithmically correlated fields. Surprisingly, they conjectured that also the Riemann zeta function belongs to this log-correlated group. While there has been huge progress in proving this conjecture, most of the current results are for integrable models. The goal of this project is to establish new analytical techniques to show that this connection holds for a large class of random matrix models, and more. In general, the broad interest of our research group lies at the interface of mathematical physics and probability, with connections to…

item.title: Incarico post-doc: Instability and pattern selection in confined active nematic fluids (Univ. NAPOLI)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-04 Fisica matematica

ctive nematic fluids exhibit instability transitions strongly conditioned by confinement geometry. The project investigates the role of boundary conditions and domain geometry in the onset of instabilities and flow pattern selection, extending results obtained for annular domains and cylindrical surfaces. Using stability and bifurcation analysis, asymptotic methods, and numerical techniques, the project will study how curvature and geometric confinement modify instability thresholds. The goal is to build a unified theoretical framework for controlling emergent patterns, with applications in confined biological systems and active microfluidic devices.

item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-12 10:00
Institution: Univ. NAPOLI, Napoli
Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-02 Algebra e geometria

The research project aims to develop a covariant Hamiltonian description of the gravitational interaction and to analyze the geometric properties of Einstein's equations for general relativity on non-globally hyperbolic manifolds. The activity focuses on three main points: 1. Global analysis of the pre-symplectic algorithm for the Palatini formulation of Einstein's equations; 2. Geometric characterization of gauge symmetries as the kernel of the pre-symplectic form; 3. Study of the quotient space geometry.

Field: Mathematics and computer science / 01/MATH-05 Analisi numerica

Numerical simulation of action potential propagation in cardiac electrophysiology is currently a highly useful tool for predictive purposes. This project builds upon the work carried out within the INNOVA project regarding arrhythmia prediction. Specifically, it aims to validate proposed risk indices and evaluate the importance of including myocardial motion and the right ventricle in the simulations. The LifeX finite element library will be used for these purposes.
